correctness.rationale: The exact inclusion-exclusion probability for each unsensed arc and the hypergeometric second-difference identity reconstruct the claimed objective and all its equality cases for n>=3, 1<=k<=n, 0<=m<=n. A separate exhaustive graph-component implementation matched 9,151 cases through n=9, while the unrestricted result is proved analytically.

value.rationale: A complete natural three-parameter intervention classification on ring-shaped contact systems with a fixed disruption budget. The sharp flat-plateau cutoff means that increasing contact failures qualitatively expands optimal deployments from balanced arcs to arbitrarily uneven arcs above a stated minimum, a nontrivial feature not implied by an informal equispacing heuristic. The result directly quantifies eventual detection probability and can be independently reproduced.
